boundaries: Exactly one primary subject kind is selected. A Product workspace may link zero or more Projects; a Project workspace binds its own Project and does not own other primary Projects.
A Goal or Work record retains its existing Project ownership. Product-wide operations may omit a Project; Project-owned operations require a selected linked Project.
A Project, Goal, Person, Team or model record does not automatically create another workspace.
One Product has one canonical operating home. Co-located Project records do not provision extra homes or duplicate Product identity.
Workspace kind and behavior specialization do not force dedicated execution, separate installation, copied runtime code or new authority.
An unselected native subject identity remains explicitly unselected. A catalog key, folder or passing validation does not admit an identity or grant native permission.
Lab Workspace names the durable scope; runtime instance names execution. Incompatible model/profile revisions require an explicit conversion.

residue_refs: Candidate semantic standing does not create native admission or authority grants.

scientific_formal.formal_expression: W = (id, revision, primary_subject, purpose_refs, scope, owners, model_binding_ref, home_refs, selections, extensions, lifecycle, challenge_route). kind(primary_subject(W)) in {Product, Project}. identity(W) != identity(primary_subject(W)). location_change(W) does not imply identity_change(W). valid_profile(W) does not imply authorized(W).
scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Lab Workspace is a durable, versioned operating scope bound to one explicitly selected primary subject of kind Product or Project. A Product workspace keeps its Product records, linked Project coordination and Work in one canonical home. A Project workspace binds one Project and may reference a Product or another declared purpose. It connects eight responsibility areas to an exact operating-model revision, accountable routes, source selections, configuration and lifecycle contracts. Workspace identity, subject identity, physical home, runtime instance and authority grants remain distinct. Shared operations and shared execution are the default; specialization does not require a runtime copy.

notation.meaning: Exact parent/local Model Instance Binding, with separately scoped authority.
Selected canonical-home manifests with their own lifecycle/recovery ownership.

testable_conditions: Both Product and Project profiles validate with exactly one matching primary subject kind.
Linked Projects and Goal ownership are explicit and wrong-scope operations refuse.
All eight responsibilities resolve to one canonical Product home.
Multiple workspaces resolve to one shared execution target without code copies.
Legacy Project profiles convert explicitly with unchanged subject and Goal membership.
Native permission gates remain enforced by the existing host.
